articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications' (Digest No.34)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications
IEE Colloquium on GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications
abstract: On-state voltage and energy lost during device switching are two of the key parameters in GTO thyristor design and operation. The trade-off between on-state voltage (V/sub TM/) and energy lost during device turn-off (E/sub off/) for a GTO thyristor is explained, and examined using lifetime control methods. Three methods are considered electron irradiation, proton irradiation and gold diffusion. Electron irradiation is examined in detail and it is shown that optimised V/sub TM/-E/sub OFF/ may be achieved for any combination of duty cycle and frequency thus providing the circuit designer with minimised average power dissipation during device operation. A comparison is made with gold diffusion and proton irradiation. From these results a suitable process is selected for lifetime control of 1200V, 300A GTO thyristors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications
abstract: Recent advances in bipolar transistor technology have been considerable. Transistors can now be applied economically and reliably to a wide range of power switching applications, many of which were impossible with other power semiconductors. The authors discuss the characteristics and application of transistors as high frequency power switches operating from supplies up to approximately 575V AC (1000V DC link maximum). Both standard triple Darlington bipolar transistors ('Triplingtons') and the newer insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBT) are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications
abstract: Auxiliary power supplies are required for operating air conditioning units, ventilation fans, lighting and battery charging. Traditionally this function has been fulfilled by motor-alternator sets. In recent years, however, GTO development, availability and price have made 3 phase GTO auxiliary inverters an attractive alternative to MA sets. GEC Traction have recently supplied a prototype 3 phase static auxiliary inverter to Hong Kong MTRC, which has been in passenger service since May 1987. Successful trials led to an order for 41, 65kVA naturally cooled static auxiliary inverters. The first of these has been in passenger service since February 1988. The authors discuss the advantages of static auxiliary supplies and examine the design features of naturally ventilated GTO auxiliary inverters. System control and performance is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications
abstract: Digitally controlled GTO choppers are now the norm for all new DC EMU equipment. This change represents a revolution in the design of propulsion equipment as dramatic as the introduction of power semiconductor devices in the 1960s. The author discusses seven recent designs of choppers using gate turn off (GTO) thyristors. Details are given of three designs that are being introduced into fleet operation on British Rail, Hong Kong MTRC and the London Docklands Light Railway.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast thyristor operation of the GTO
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications
abstract: The GTO was developed to meet designers demands for a device which combined the high voltage/high current capabilities of the thyristor with the transistors ability to turn off a current via a control electrode. The GTO is, basically, a thyristor in which the gains of the internal transistors have been carefully adjusted so that a negative gate voltage will divert part of the on state current into the gate unlatching the device and turning it off. The author examines the limitations and losses of GTO thyristor operation, and applications of its use are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Initial investigation into use of GTO's in resonant circuit topologies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on GTO's, Rival Devices and Applications
abstract: The authors investigate the use of GTO's in resonant circuit topologies for industrial applications. Details of the design and analysis of typical circuits will be given for the following circuits: (1) a resonant buck type DC/DC converter operating at 60 kHz with an output of 200 W at 60 V; (2) a resonant fly-back DC/DC converter operating at 60 kHz to supply a 5 V, 4 A output; (3) an induction cooling power supply based on a class E type amplifier of 500 W, using a GTO at a nominal frequency of 60 kHz; (4) a high efficiency class E tuned power oscillator operating at 100 W but at frequencies in the megahertz region using an RF power MOSFET. The analysis made use of the circuit simulation package PSPICE and prototype units based on these designs are being constructed. Progress on the evaluation of these prototypes is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
